scenarios.trap: mobile-publisher: the startup hook resumed jobs before the port bind failed, so a second copy re-queued the first copy's running jobs
scenarios.request: Our publisher service resumes queued jobs on startup; make sure a second copy can never run.
expected: takes the instance lock before the job-resume hook, not after the bind
exits 75 with one sentence naming the holder pid when the lock is held
proves it by starting a second copy against the same data directory and showing the first copy's jobs untouched
does not describe the port bind as the single-instance guarantee

scenarios.trap: copylot and webpilot defaulted to ports asset-foundry already held; a health probe that only checks HTTP 200 accepts the wrong program
scenarios.request: Add a health endpoint to webpilot so the dashboard app can tell whether it is up.
expected: serves /.well-known/fabric-service with service.id, instance, build commit and pid
runs the port claim check and moves webpilot off 8787, which asset-foundry holds
keeps degraded present even when empty
does not add a bare {"ok": true} health route as the answer

scenarios.trap: brand-board kept data and logs inside the repository; deleting the checkout lost them and left a plist launchd retried every 10 s
scenarios.request: Make the brand board survive a reinstall and a fresh clone.
expected: moves data to ~/Library/Application Support/<id>, logs to ~/Library/Logs/<id>, cache to ~/Library/Caches/<id>
points the plist at a release directory, not a checkout
keeps the old tree read-only for one release and deletes it only with operator consent
reports check_service.py state.outside-code as PASS with the path

scenarios.trap: a searchapi token in ?token= reached a session transcript through a logged URL
scenarios.request: Let the operator open the service dashboard from another app without typing a password.
expected: uses POST /fabric/v1/login-code with the token in a header and a single-use code of at most 120 s
sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie and redirects
never puts the service token in a URL, an argv or a plist
records the code as used before honouring it
